risks.title: Preflight smoke test mutated the pristine base checkpoint in place
risks.evidence: Fix present (_stage_writable_checkpoint_for_smoke_test) with regression test. Independently re-demonstrated this review: loading the real parent through the production path mutated the STAGED copy (372,591,597 -> 124,288,226 bytes, .old backup created) while the pristine parent stayed byte-identical at 0da2c00a... The staging discipline is both necessary and working.
risks.required_action: None.

risks.title: resume had no guard against re-entering a COMPLETED/FAILED run
risks.evidence: is_resume rejection present and tested; re-confirmed in this review's 32-test launch-guard suite.
risks.required_action: None.

risks.title: Launch guard never checked code-commit drift since prepare
risks.evidence: Fix present and demonstrated live again this review: each of my own commits invalidated the then-current prepared run, and the guard refused it every time. Working as designed.
risks.required_action: Prepare LAST, immediately before launching -- any later commit (including documentation) invalidates a prepared run.

risks.title: TrainingSessionState.global_step is always 0
risks.opus_classification: SAFE TO RELABEL AND DEFER -- relabelling now done
risks.evidence: Confirmed always 0, never assigned. Metadata only: not read by training, scheduler, or resume logic (resume keys off cumulative_epoch + latest_checkpoint_dir). The original audit hoped optimizer.iterations was the real authoritative counter; this review proved it is ALSO always 0 (see R-019), so no authoritative step counter exists anywhere in this architecture.
risks.required_action: Done: labels no longer claim what does not exist. A redundant synthetic counter was deliberately NOT added -- it would be write-only noise.
risks.accepted_risk: No step-level resumability exists or is claimed. Shard-level resumability is real and sufficient.

risks.title: resume-proof's 'global_step_continued_not_restarted' actually re-tests epoch continuity
risks.evidence: Confirmed verbatim. Renamed to session_boundary_epoch_continued_not_restarted; an explicit optimizer_state_continued: False plus an explanatory note are now emitted. The preflight check that consumed it (optimizer_scheduler_state_serialization) was renamed resume_state_continuity and its live output now states plainly what is and is not carried across checkpoints.
risks.required_action: None.

risks.title: random_seed could diverge between persisted state and resume invocation
risks.opus_classification: RESOLVED (fixed in the prior review pass, re-verified here)
risks.evidence: run_training_session raises ValueError on seed mismatch, mirroring configuration_hash. Scope bounded precisely: epoch_seed feeds only the container's --seed (intra-shard shuffling); it cannot change shard selection (fixed at prepare time) and there is no augmentation. Reproducibility gap, not data-integrity.
risks.required_action: Use the same --seed on every start/resume for a run (now enforced automatically).

risks.title: Launch-time shard-integrity check was self-referential; test overlap never re-checked
risks.opus_classification: RESOLVED (fixed prior pass, independently verified here)
risks.evidence: recompute_real_shard_hash() reads every real lap-0 shard file and independently reproduces the hash. Tamper test passes (overwrite a real shard, leave summary untouched -> detected). Verified no false positive on the real 171-shard set: rehash == frozen manifest hash (e12796a0...). Symmetric test-manifest overlap check added.
risks.required_action: None.

risks.title: verify_checkpoint only validates zip structure, never a functional load
risks.evidence: This review functionally loaded the REAL PARENT checkpoint through the production code path (management.load_model_from_directory) on a staged copy: model_new10, input (None,None,64,1), output (None,None,457), 28 layers, 31,033,929 parameters. Also functionally loaded two real pilot checkpoints. All succeeded.
risks.required_action: None. verify_checkpoint's cheap structural check remains adequate per-shard; a genuinely unloadable checkpoint is still caught one shard later by the existing epoch_failed safe stop.
risks.accepted_risk: One shard of wasted wall-clock in the unlikely structural-pass / functional-fail case.

risks.title: Document/writer-level leakage cannot be excluded for 7/11 collections
risks.opus_classification: UNCHANGED -- correctly classified as scientific interpretation, not launch safety
risks.evidence: Exact line-level leakage independently re-measured as 0 across all 171 real shard files (train-vs-validation AND train-vs-test). Document/writer overlap is unknowable -- no such identifier exists in the source data. Not classified as proven exact leakage.
risks.required_action: Disclose explicitly in any per-collection or aggregate CER claim.
risks.accepted_risk: Data-collection limitation, not a code defect. Affects CER interpretation and publication claims only.

risks.required_action: Defer to a data-quality workstream.

risks.title: TelemetrySampler thread has no exception guard beyond ImportError
risks.opus_classification: UNCHANGED, but now slightly more consequential

risks.title: No checkpoint retention or disk monitoring; plan exceeded free disk
risks.opus_classification: CAPACITY RESOLVED; hardening gap remains, ACCEPTED
risks.evidence: Independently measured: 322.31 GB free (operator claim verified, not assumed). Per-shard cost re-derived from individual epoch directories rather than an average: 745,315,540 bytes, constant to ~1KB across epochs 1/7/14/22. Full 171-shard plan 127.44 GB + 0.75 GB staged parent + 0.15 GB shards = ~128.3 GB. Reserve ~194 GB (60%). Docker's 74.75 GB sits on C:, not D: (verified via DockerRootDir and a D: VHDX scan). Retention and mid-run monitoring still absent; disk-full path analysed at code level -- mkstemp/os.replace means a loud crash, never corruption of the prior good file.
risks.required_action: None blocking. Implement retention + mid-run disk checks before reusing this workflow for longer or repeated campaigns.
risks.accepted_risk: No retention policy, no mid-run disk monitor, no live disk-full test -- accepted for this run on the strength of a 60% measured reserve.

risks.title: Optimizer momentum and LR-schedule state do not survive ANY shard boundary -- and the repository was recording the opposite as fact
risks.severity: HIGH as a finding; NOT BLOCKING as a consequence
risks.impact: Two independent mechanisms each destroy optimizer state. (1) SAVE SIDE, primary: custom_callback.py::_save_model saves tf.keras.models.clone_model(...) output -- a fresh, UNCOMPILED model with only copied weights -- so every checkpoint ever written contains zero optimizer state. Confirmed by loading the real parent: the result has no .optimizer attribute at all. (2) LOAD SIDE, secondary: main.py:103-119 unconditionally rebuilds schedule+optimizer and calls model.compile() every invocation. Effective regime is near-constant-LR fine-tuning at 1e-4 with Adam re-warming each shard, NOT one long decaying schedule. Separately and more seriously, the repository was ASSERTING the opposite in durable evidence: CheckpointEntry.optimizer_state_present/scheduler_state_present were True on all 47 real pilot entries, training_session.py's docstring claimed full optimizer state including iterations was restored, and learning_rate_policy read 'constant_0.0001_decay_0.99'. A run started under those labels would have carried permanently false provenance.
risks.evidence: Synthetic model, real pinned container, real GPU, never the corpus. BEFORE SAVE iterations=12 lr=0.0009702991 momentum=[0.00583729,-0.03682394,0.1461488]; AFTER RELOAD (no recompile) iterations=12 lr=0.0009702991 momentum bit-identical; AFTER +1 EPOCH iterations=16 lr=0.0009605961; AFTER RELOAD+RECOMPILE (Loghi path) iterations=0 lr=0.0010000000; AFTER +1 EPOCH iterations=4. Keras preserves optimizer state perfectly; Loghi does not use it.
risks.mitigation: NOT a launch blocker: this is the unconditional behaviour of every invocation including all 22 pilot epochs, and the pilot empirically validated it (val_CER 0.55 -> 0.169, monotonic). Weights carry correctly; resume works via ArchiveTrust's externally-tracked counters. FIXED the false records: optimizer_state_present/scheduler_state_present now False with evidence; module docstring corrected with measurements; resume-proof field renamed + explicit optimizer_state_continued: False; preflight check renamed resume_state_continuity with an honest message; learning_rate_policy corrected (changing the configuration hash, hence the re-prepare).
risks.status: behaviour accepted and validated by pilot evidence; false records corrected
risks.verification_method: Real GPU experiment in the pinned container plus direct reading of custom_callback.py and main.py. Zero new training.
risks.required_action: Operator awareness: expect 171 chained short fine-tunes at ~constant LR. To decay LR late in training, lower --learning_rate manually between resume invocations -- nothing does it automatically.

risks.title: Crash recovery was impossible -- the documented recovery path could never work
risks.severity: HIGH -- would have been BLOCKING if not fixed
risks.impact: A crash (power loss, reboot, Ctrl+C, killed container) leaves run_state.json at status='running' with no process attached. The launch guard rejected RUNNING/STOPPING unconditionally, for resume as well as start -- so failure_recovery_runbook.md's own documented recovery ('...then resume --run <dir> --confirm-full-corpus-run') could never succeed. On a multi-day unattended run the operator's only escape was hand-editing run_state.json. The original audit missed this because it reasoned about the runbook rather than executing it.
risks.evidence: Direct simulation: crash state status='running' pid=23376 -> guard verdict 'An active run already exists ... with status running' -> RESUME BLOCKED = True.
risks.mitigation: Fixed fail-closed. looks_like_a_crashed_run() uses telemetry/status.json (rewritten every ~5s during a container run; stale >300s = writer gone), deliberately NOT run_state.json's per-shard heartbeat which is legitimately ~8 min old mid-shard. Crashed+no flag -> still blocked with an actionable message; crashed+--force-resume-after-crash -> recovers from the last verified checkpoint; LIVE+flag -> still blocked; missing/malformed telemetry -> fails closed; `start` can never use the override. Five tests.
risks.verification_method: Simulated the failure, fixed, then verified all five branches by test.
risks.required_action: None. Operator: after a crash, check docker ps, then resume --force-resume-after-crash.

risks.title: Full-corpus preparation never produced trainer-consumable data -- the run could not have trained at all
risks.impact: cmd_prepare produced Parquet shard manifests and handed them to the container as --train_list. Upstream data/manager.py:257 reads a training list as UTF-8 text (<image_path>TAB<ground_truth>) and cannot parse Parquet. Separately, the line images were never extracted for the full corpus at all -- no prepared-data/ existed in any prepared run, whereas the pilot had 10,999 PNGs plus train_list.txt. Every prepared run, across all six preparations and three audit passes, was in a PREPARED_NOT_STARTED state it could never successfully have left. The readiness decision of CONDITIONAL GO was therefore based on a run that could not train.
risks.evidence: First real shard attempt (Gate 4, operator-authorised, bounded to one shard): stop_reason=epoch_failed, 53s runtime vs ~482s expected, epoch_output/epoch_1/ empty, 0 shards completed. The staged parent checkpoint converted normally first (372,591,597 -> 124,288,226 bytes), proving it died on data rather than on the model. See gate4_first_shard_review_record.md.
risks.why_missed: The preflight smoke test used the PILOT's probe lists (real text files, real extracted images), so it exercised a data path the full run never uses -- passing 21/21 four times while the real shard input was unreadable. The dry-run stops before the trainer by design. The audits verified shard CONTENTS exhaustively (line IDs, overlap, duplicates, hashes, determinism) but never that shards were in a FORMAT the container could consume. Content correctness and interface correctness are different properties; only the former was ever checked.
risks.mitigation: Fixed in commit cbf9b21. New shard_training_data.py calls the existing, pilot-proven prepare_loghi_training_data() adapter and solves two problems the pilot never faced: (1) laps triplicate images -- 3 laps over the same 562,123 lines would extract ~1.7M files/~250GB, so images are extracted once from the lap-0 union and shared; (2) the container mounts a list file's PARENT at /lists, forcing a flat pool layout. The pool is keyed by (dataset hash, shard-plan hash) so reuse is verifiable and re-preparation does not re-extract ~82GB. The preflight smoke test now prefers a probe cut from the full-corpus pool. _run_session refuses a run prepared before this wiring rather than failing ~50s into a container start.
risks.verification_method: Real production interface, not unit tests alone: a bounded pool built from real shard data fed to the real pinned container via ContainerEpochRunner -- exit_code 0, train_cer 0.662, val_cer 0.538, valid checkpoint written, pristine parent hash unchanged. Plus 12 new unit tests covering the lap-triplication trap, container list format, image resolvability, and pool reuse keying. Full suite 2370 passed.
risks.required_action: None for the defect. Standing lesson: no readiness decision should be issued again until real artifacts have been fed to the real trainer interface at least once.
